new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (753 pp., De Gruyter 2023, OAPEN mirror). Printed p. 177 = PDF page 194, running head "The Language of the Caucasian Albanians 177", within ch. 4 (Gippert & Schulze; chapter DOI https://doi.org/10.1515/9783110794687-004 printed on its opening page). Sect. 2.2.3 "Syllable structure and prosody" ends with the sentence exactly as quoted: "Nothing is known about the prosodic features of Albanian. Nevertheless, the strong presence of enclitic (in parts also proclitic) elements suggests that the language was characterised by some kind of stress accent." The rest of the section is on syllable structure (cluster avoidance, anaptyxis/metathesis in loans, status of pharyngeal <ʕ>); sect. 2.2.4…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The primary describers state explicitly that nothing is known about Caucasian Albanian prosody; they infer only that the language probably had a stress accent (from the abundance of clitics), without any statement of where it fell. A passing remark in ch. 5 (Schulze & Gippert, p. 255) that clitics came to stand 'after the first accented syllable of the verbal complex' is an inference used to explain endoclisis, not a placement rule.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the source says the prosody is unknown.
new_statements.domain_note: Extinct corpus language (7th-c. palimpsests, Mingachevir inscriptions); stress is not recoverable from the script. The only indirect evidence cited is clitic placement in the verbal complex (word/verbal-complex level).
new_statements.identity_note: Aghwan = Caucasian Albanian = Old Udi (ISO xag), the language of the 7th-c. Sinai palimpsests (Sin. N 13, N 55) and the Mingachevir inscriptions; an extinct Lezgic language, ancestor of or sister to modern Udi (udii1243). The statement is about the palimpsest language as a whole (no dialects distinguished). The handbook chapter is the same authors' (Gippert & Schulze) condensation of the 2008 Brepols edition's grammar sketch.

new_statements.quote: It seems likely that cases like these induced a preference for the clitic to enter into a position after the first accented syllable of the verbal complex, which was then generalised. This process may have been triggered by the existence of infixed presents of the type of ʒe-le-xa- 'fixing' (vs. past ʒexa- etc.) in Albanian.

new_statements.relation_note: Compatible with the catalog's only statement (ch. 4 of the same handbook, p. 177: 'Nothing is known about the prosodic features of Albanian.. some kind of stress accent' inferred from clitics). Ch. 5 adds only the further inference that the accented syllable that served as clitic host stood at the beginning of the verbal complex; it gives no placement rule and does not change the 'unclear' status. The catalog record for Caucasian Albanian has an empty rule; nothing here fills it.
new_statements.rule_in_words: No word-stress rule is given for Caucasian Albanian. The only accent-related sentence is a diachronic inference: Udi endoclitics were generalised to the slot after the 'first accented syllable of the verbal complex', which presupposes an accent early in the verbal complex (on the negator te-, a preverb, or a monosyllabic stem) in the Albanian-to-Udi transition. Nothing on where stress falls in ordinary words.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the chapter notes that in Albanian clitics always follow the verbal form or another meaningful element (bowq̇a-za 'I want', biq̇ay-ne 'he seized', ta-daġē-ne 'he gave'), whereas Udi inserts them (bu-za-q̇sa, bi-ne-q̇e, ta-ne-di); the shared constellations are monosyllabic stems (CA pē-ne ~ Udi pi-ne), imperfect auxiliary CA -hē ~ Udi -i after the clitic (bow-ne-hē ~ bu-ne-i), and negator + clitic (CA te-ne-bow ~ Udi te-ne-bu).
new_statements.identity_note: Caucasian Albanian (Aghwan) is the written Old Udi of the Mt Sinai palimpsests and the Mingachevir inscriptions (c. 5th-8th c.); Schulze 2001 describes modern Udi (Vartashen and Nij dialects, Glottolog udii1243), the only living descendant, whose Azeri-influenced final stress is a modern development per Schulze himself.

readall_conflicts: No source states a word-stress placement for Caucasian Albanian. The handbook ch. 4 (Gippert & Schulze 2023: 177, already in the catalog) says nothing is known of Albanian prosody and infers only 'some kind of stress accent' from the clitics; ch. 5 (Schulze & Gippert 2023: 255) adds the diachronic inference that clitics generalised to the slot after 'the first accented syllable of the verbal complex'. The one mild tension is Schulze's 2001 parenthesis that 'historically, Udi had its words stressed on the first or second syllable', an unsourced pre-decipherment reconstruction, against the 2023 handbook's explicit 'nothing is known'; the two are not contradictory in substance (an early-syllable accent hosting clitics fits both), but the 2001 remark should not be entered as an attested Albanian rule. Schulze 2001's modern-Udi description (Azeri-like final stress with clitic-induced retraction) concerns a different, later language state.
